title: Choosing the Best FBR POS for a Lahore Restaurant
metaDescription: How to choose an FBR POS for a Lahore restaurant — the features that actually matter for dine-in, takeaway, and delivery, and the questions to ask any vendor.
content:
Why choosing a restaurant POS is its own decision

Picking an FBR POS for a Lahore restaurant is not the same as picking one for a shop. A restaurant adds items mid-meal, splits bills, applies service charge, and turns tables fast — all while every sale still has to reach FBR IRIS with a QR-coded invoice. The best system for you is the one that keeps compliance invisible to your staff during a rush, not the one with the longest feature list.

This guide is about how to choose well, so you do not end up replacing the system in six months.

The features that actually matter

  • Live FBR IRIS integration — verified, not claimed. Ask to watch a real invoice validate on the FBR portal.
  • Offline billing — queues sales during an outage and syncs with original timestamps.
  • Fast order handling — split bills, item modifications, and voids without slowing the table.
  • Kitchen display (KDS) support — orders flow to the kitchen while staying linked to the FBR invoice.
  • Correct tax mapping for F&B items and service charge.

Questions to ask any vendor

  1. Can you show me a live invoice verifying on the FBR portal right now?
  2. What happens to orders if my internet drops mid-service?
  3. How are voids and modifications reported to FBR?
  4. How do you handle FBR rule changes — do I update, or do you?
  5. What is the total monthly cost, including support?

A real example

A Lahore restaurant in Johar Town chose the cheapest POS without testing voids. Cancelled orders stayed in IRIS as valid sales, inflating reported revenue until an accountant caught it. The lesson: test the awkward cases — voids, splits, outages — before you commit, not after.

Making the call

Shortlist two or three systems, run a real dinner service on each if you can, and weight compliance reliability above flashy extras. Once you choose, our guide to FBR POS for restaurants covers the setup, and the compliance checklist keeps you on track after go-live.

faqs.question: What features matter most for a Lahore restaurant POS?
faqs.answer: A live FBR IRIS integration, offline billing that queues and syncs, fast handling of split bills and modifications, and kitchen-display support. Compliance plus speed at the table is the combination that matters.

faqs.question: How do I verify a vendor's FBR integration is real?
faqs.answer: Ask to see a live invoice verify on the FBR portal, not a screenshot. A genuine integration produces a QR that resolves to a real IRIS record; a vague 'FBR ready' claim is not the same thing.

faqs.question: Do I need expensive hardware for a restaurant POS?
faqs.answer: No. A compliant POS runs on tablets or a phone, so you can take orders at the table. The cost is in the software and integration, not specialised terminals.

faqs.question: Can the POS handle a Friday-night rush if the internet drops?
faqs.answer: A good one queues orders locally during an outage and syncs them to FBR IRIS with original timestamps when the connection returns, so service never stops.
